task.description:
REWORK ITERATION 2 of 3, and it is small. The step-04 re-gate confirmed **all seven of G1..G7 CLOSED**, re-derived from the files rather than from your report, and accounted for every one of your 19 deletions as a required rewrite-in-place with nothing weakened. Neither b13a523 nor 808e2e1 is reverted; this is additive on top.

The FAIL is on **G8**, which you yourself raised and correctly did not act on. Three smaller items are folded in by ORCH.

**G8 (GATING) — the PR body template now instructs an agent to write a false-looking PASS.** `docs/agents/protocols/GIT_MERGE.md` step 7's template line 178 reads `- mix test: PASS`. REVIEWER's ruling, which ORCH accepts, is that this run did not merely EXPOSE the problem, it CAUSED it: before G3, writing PASS next to 13-15 failures was an unsanctioned claim an agent reached via the count-matching R1 now forbids — an agent error. After G3 redefined 'green' as 'no failure attributable to this branch', that same PASS is the PRESCRIBED label for a run that reported failures. The run converted an agent error into an instructed output, which is a weakening, and this gate existed to confirm none occurred.

  It is also exactly the shape core-directives' 'Never Call a Red Pipeline OK Without a Source' forbids: G3 supplies the justification but parks it in a handoff JSON, while step 7 emits the bare label to the PR with no pointer. Note the asymmetry that makes this worse than the other artefacts this run touched — every other one is read by agents who will follow a pointer; **the PR body is the one read by a human who will not.**

  Fix: amend the template so the test line cannot be written as a bare verdict when the run is non-zero. It must carry the actual counts AND the attribution basis — which of R1's three routes was used and for what — so a human reading only the PR can see that failures occurred and why they were judged not this branch's. Keep it short enough that an agent will actually fill it in; a template nobody completes is worse than a blunt one. Apply the same treatment to any sibling line in that template that can go stale the same way (check the surrounding lines rather than assuming this is the only one).

**G9 (folded in) — G1's mandate can be voided by an empty set.** `.claude/agents/test-design-validator.md` now requires applying 'at least one of TEST-DESIGNER's *reported* mutants'. If TEST-DESIGNER reports none, the mandate has nothing to bind to. The producer's own role file, `.claude/agents/test-designer.md` (its WF-03 regression-test paragraph, currently around lines 49-51), still says only that the test must be shown to fail against pre-fix code and verified rather than asserted — correct as far as it goes, and NOT permissive, which is why REVIEWER ruled it non-gating. But it is silent on the new-code case. Amend it so that when the pre-fix failure is 'the code under test did not exist', TEST-DESIGNER MUST produce and report at least one mutant of the shipped logic with its measured counts. That makes the validator's mandate always have a subject. Cross-reference WF-03's subsection rather than restating the technique.

**G10 (folded in) — the G5 defect survives one level up.** `core-directives.md`'s Unblock-Everything 'Scope boundary' paragraph (around line 247) still tells the discovering agent to 'register it under docs/issues/ISS-NNNN.yaml and, if a gh remote is configured and reachable, file it as a real GitHub issue too'. That is the same instruction G5 removed from WF-02/WF-04, and it is doubly wrong now: only ORCH calls the queue, and issue ids are no longer chosen by anyone — they come back from register_task as issue_ref. REVIEWER ruled this non-gating because precedence reaches the right answer (protocols rank 4 beat core-directives rank 5). ORCH is folding it in anyway, and the reason is worth stating: 'benign because precedence saves it' is the same reasoning that made G1 dangerous in the opposite direction, and this doc set should not carry a known-wrong instruction on the strength of another rule out-ranking it. Amend it to report-for-filing, consistent with ISSUE_QUEUE.md, and drop the ISS-NNNN naming.

**G11 (folded in, trivial) — readability.** G4's cross-reference clause was spliced between a noun and its defining apposition in the Scope boundary paragraph, producing two consecutive em-dash parentheticals. Re-flow that sentence. No meaning change.

Do NOT revert or rewrite anything from b13a523 or 808e2e1 beyond what these four items require. Do NOT touch code, tests, `docs/issues/`, `docs/requirements.yaml`, `docs/status/`, or ORCH's `handoffs/registry.json` and `handoffs/orchestrator.log`. Another session may be active in this checkout — re-read rather than overwrite if a file changes under you.
acceptance_criteria: G8 -- GIT_MERGE.md step 7's template can no longer be completed as a bare test verdict: it requires the actual counts and which of R1's three attribution routes was used and for what. Quote the before and after. Sibling template lines checked for the same staleness and amended if affected
G8 -- the amended template is short enough to be plausibly filled in every run; state why you believe it will be, rather than asserting it

G9 -- .claude/agents/test-designer.md requires producing and reporting at least one mutant with measured counts when the pre-fix failure is non-existence, cross-referencing WF-03 rather than restating the technique, so the validator's mandate always has a subject

G10 -- core-directives.md's Scope boundary no longer instructs the discovering agent to register an ISS-NNNN file or call gh; it reports for filing, consistent with ISSUE_QUEUE.md, with no id chosen by the agent
G11 -- the spliced sentence is re-flowed with no meaning change
Nothing from the prior two commits is weakened or removed beyond what these four items require -- verify with git diff and account for every deletion
Only the three files in owned_modules and your own handoff are modified

result.summary:
All four items (G8 gating, G9/G10/G11 folded in) are closed. 37 insertions, 9 deletions across the three owned_modules files; nothing from b13a523 or 808e2e1 is reverted or weakened, and every one of the 9 deletions is a rewrite-in-place at a site one of these four items required amending.

G8 -- CLOSED. `docs/agents/protocols/GIT_MERGE.md` step 7 --body template.
BEFORE (2 lines, both deleted):
  `- mix test: PASS`
  `- SECURITY-REVIEWER: PASS | out of scope`
AFTER:
  `- mix test: <passed> passed, <N> failed, 0 attributable to this branch`
  `  (attribution route <1|2|3>: <one clause naming the evidence>; recorded in`
  `  handoffs/<run-id>/)`
  `- SECURITY-REVIEWER: PASS | out of scope (<one clause: why no tenant-data path>)`
The verdict slot is gone: there is no longer a token an agent can write instead of the counts. The line cannot be completed at all without (a) the real passed/failed numbers and (b) which of R1's three attribution routes was used and against what evidence. A one-sentence-plus warning under the fenced template states that green here means no failure attributable to this branch, that a bare PASS next to a non-zero count is forbidden by core-directives' 'Never Call a Red Pipeline OK Without a Source', that if <N> is 0 the agent writes `0 failed` and drops the parenthetical, and -- the point of the whole item -- that the attribution must appear IN the PR body because the PR body is the one artefact a human reads without following a pointer.

SIBLING LINES CHECKED, per the AC, rather than assuming the test line was the only one. Four lines in the Validation block. `mix compile --warnings-as-errors: PASS` -- left unchanged and the warning says so explicitly: that gate genuinely is zero-tolerance, so a bare PASS there is a complete statement, not a label standing in for an off-PR justification. `SECURITY-REVIEWER: PASS | out of scope` -- AMENDED, it is the same shape: 'out of scope' is a judgement made elsewhere and a human reading the PR alone cannot tell whether a tenant-data path was considered and cleared or never looked at. It now carries a one-clause reason. `RELEASE-VALIDATOR: PASS` -- left unchanged: that role's verdict is a re-derivation over the acceptance criteria named two lines above in the same body, so the PR already carries its subject; adding a slot there would be cost without a reader-visible gain.

G8 second AC -- WHY THE AMENDED TEMPLATE WILL ACTUALLY BE FILLED IN, argued rather than asserted. Three reasons, in order of weight. (1) EVERY SLOT IS ALREADY IN THE AGENT'S HAND AT STEP 7 -- it is transcription, not new work. `<passed>`/`<N>` are the two numbers printed by the `mix test` the same agent ran forty lines earlier at step 5d, and step 5d as amended by G3 already REQUIRES the route and its evidence to have been determined before the agent is permitted to continue past that step. An agent that reaches step 7 legitimately cannot fail to have this information; the template asks it to copy what it already wrote, and the warning tells it so in as many words ('you already have both from step 5d; copy them'). The failure mode that kills templates -- a field requiring analysis the author has not done -- does not exist here. (2) IT IS SHORT AND BOUNDED. One line plus a two-line parenthetical, four fill-ins, each a value or a single clause; no free prose, no minimum length, and the common case is shorter still, since <N>=0 collapses it to `<passed> passed, 0 failed` with the parenthetical dropped -- so the extra burden is borne only by runs that actually have failures to explain, which is exactly where it is warranted. (3) THE ALTERNATIVE IS NOT AVAILABLE. Skipping a slot leaves a literal `<passed>` or `<1|2|3>` angle-bracket placeholder in a published PR body, which is conspicuous to the next reader in a way that a wrong-but-plausible `PASS` never was. Filling it correctly is the cheapest path, not the most diligent one. The honest residual risk: an agent could write plausible-looking numbers it did not measure. No template can prevent that, and it is not what this item was about -- G8 was that the template PRESCRIBED the false-looking output; it no longer does.

G9 -- CLOSED. `.claude/agents/test-designer.md`, appended to the WF-03 regression-test paragraph (the prior text is unchanged; this is 10 added lines, 0 deleted). Where the pre-fix failure is that the code under test did not exist, that check 'is trivially satisfied and proves nothing' and TEST-DESIGNER MUST additionally mutate the shipped logic and REPORT at least one mutant with its measured counts (which tests failed, how many) in its handoff, reverting each mutant and verifying the revert. It cross-references WF-03's subsection by its exact heading -- 'When the pre-fix failure is "the code under test does not exist"' -- with 'follow it there, it is not restated here', so the technique lives in one place. The empty-set hole is closed explicitly and in the producer's own file: reporting no mutants for a non-existence case is named as a step failure, with the reason stated (TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR must re-apply one of YOUR reported mutants, so an empty set leaves its mandate nothing to act on) and the consequence stated (a FAIL at that gate). The validator's mandate now always has a subject.

G10 -- CLOSED. `core-directives.md` Scope boundary. The instruction to 'register it under `docs/issues/ISS-NNNN.yaml` and, if a `gh` remote is configured and reachable, file it as a real GitHub issue too' is gone. It now reads 'report the finding to ORCH per `docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md`, which is what makes it visible work', followed by 'You do NOT call the queue or `gh` yourself and you do NOT choose an issue id; only ORCH allocates ids, and a discovering agent filing directly is what reintroduces the id-collision class that rule exists to prevent.' No id shape appears anywhere in the paragraph. This matches the wording G5 put into WF-02 Step 4 item 3 and WF-04, and matches ISSUE_QUEUE.md. The pointer to 'No Issue Left Local-Only' is kept because that section carries the PRINCIPLE (a defect that never becomes visible work is invisible to the next run), which the Scope boundary is invoking; ISSUE_QUEUE.md is now the procedural authority.

G11 -- CLOSED, no meaning change. The em-dash pair now brackets only 'unrelated, not blocking your acceptance criteria' -- restored as the sole apposition defining 'a defect you merely notice', which is what it was before G4 spliced into it. G4's clause is not deleted or reworded: the same sentence, same words ('for a test failure, which side of this line it falls on is decided by "Failure Attribution Is Structural, Never By Count-Matching" below, not by judgement'), same bold, now stands as its own sentence at the end of the paragraph, where no nesting can mis-scope it. R1's reciprocal pointer back to the Scope boundary (added by G4) is untouched and still resolves.

DELETION ACCOUNTING -- 9 deletions, all accounted for, none removing a rule. `git diff --numstat`: test-designer.md 10/0, core-directives.md 9/7, GIT_MERGE.md 18/2. The 2 in GIT_MERGE.md are the two template lines quoted above under G8, each replaced in place by a longer form of itself. The 7 in core-directives.md are the entire old Scope-boundary body, rewritten in place for G10 (the ISS-NNNN/gh instruction) and G11 (the re-flow); of those 7, 2 carried G4's clause -- re-added verbatim as its own sentence -- and 1 carried the 'No Issue Left Local-Only' pointer, which is also re-added. Nothing else in either file is touched. test-designer.md is purely additive. Spot-checked that the artefacts of the prior two commits survive: GIT_MERGE.md's Precondition 'What reported green means here' paragraph with the 13-15 measurement, step 5d's attribution warning block and its re-qualified 'If FAIL (i.e. at least one failure is attributable to this branch, or is unattributed)' terminator, step 2's R2 pointer, and core-directives' three-route R1 -- all present and unmodified.

SCOPE. `git status --porcelain` before commit shows exactly the three owned_modules files plus my own handoff. I did not touch code, tests, docs/issues/, docs/requirements.yaml, docs/status/, handoffs/registry.json, or handoffs/orchestrator.log. This step is a pipeline-doc rework with no requirement in scope, so there is no requirement status to flip and no status-history event to append -- appending one would be inventing an event for a requirement that does not exist. completed_at was read from the clock via `date -u`, not from memory.
result.next_action: ORCH re-gates at REVIEWER. That re-gate should be narrow: confirm (a) GIT_MERGE.md step 7's test line has no verdict token left to write and cannot be completed without counts plus route-and-evidence, (b) the sibling-line decisions are right -- compile left bare as zero-tolerance, SECURITY-REVIEWER given a reason, RELEASE-VALIDATOR left bare -- and (c) core-directives' Scope boundary and test-designer.md's non-existence clause say what ISSUE_QUEUE.md and WF-03 say. G1-G7 were re-derived as closed at step 04 and are not re-opened by this iteration. Not pushed, per instruction; ORCH owns the push and the registry/log entries.
